correctness.rationale: The graph and operator are unambiguous and bounded. The Weyl finite-rank argument fixes the essential band. Every square-summable band eigenvector vanishes on exterior rays, so interior Dirichlet sine modes and one amplitude-sum constraint yield every embedded eigenvalue with exact multiplicity. For exterior energies, the explicitly solved recurrence yields a symmetric \(2\times2\) junction Schur complement whose parity eigenvalues have derivative at least 1; their exact \(E=2\) limits prove one versus two bound pairs and the sole threshold exception. Bipartite symmetry gives negative energies. The independent checker passed 182 direct residual, finite-matrix and scalar-root assertions; numeric truncations are not relied upon for exhaustive conclusions.

value.rationale: The two-junction construction is the first nontrivial finite-separation extension of one kinetic singularity. Its complete point-spectrum classification answers the natural physical question of how a second zero-potential junction changes localization: a whole exactly counted internal BIC ladder appears, while an odd exterior bound pair is absent only at one minimal geometry, with a genuine threshold resonance there. This is a structural family-wide fact relevant to localized excitations and spectral engineering, not a cheap renaming or parameter substitution. The proof also identifies the single-junction energy recovered as junction separation grows. The result does not claim an experimental implementation or generalization to metric graphs. The significance is the complete discrete crossover and multiplicity classification, not the generic existence of a local-symmetry BIC in two-junction geometries.
